reporting-org.narrative: Global Network of People Living with HIV (GNP+)

description.narrative: The Love Alliance, a new five-year programme (2021-2025), is based on an unwavering commitment to protecting, promoting and fulfilling sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) globally, unifying people who use drugs, sex workers and LGBTIQ+ movements, and amplifying the diversity of voices in these communities. Funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Love Alliance brings together national thought leaders GALZ, SANPUD and Sisonke, regional grantmakers UHAI EASHRI, GNP+, ISDAO and ARASA with the global network of people living with HIV (GNP+) and the Netherlands-based administrative lead Aidsfonds. Together, we advocate for adequate levels of funding and for taking truly human rights-based programmes to scale. We take this opportunity to prioritise and invest in challenging the structural barriers of underfunding, criminalisation and exclusion of us in all our diversity.

title.narrative: L1.1: communities use systems and tools for their accountability requests to decision makers 2024

description.narrative: By partnering with two registered feminist organizations, Partner has successfully pushed for the issues experienced by transgender women to be part of a more politically accepted agenda for the Egyptian government, enhancing the changes for the adoption of recommendations that will have a positive impact on transgender women. The strategic litigation case will bring an intersection with right to health that has the potential to change the realities of members of the community in detention centers.

title.narrative: L1.1: Communities use systems and tools for their accountability requests to decision makers.

description.narrative: Due to strengthened collaboration across North Africa, partners in Morocco were able to help nascent Trans movements in Egypt document violations against the trans community in Egypt’s UPR, especially those in detention centres. This is a significant step to the region’s exchange of knowledge and experience when it comes to mobilizing legal instruments of accountability.

comment.narrative: The use of legal, referral, and digital security tools enabled communities to document cases safely and engage more confidently with service providers and institutions, while seed-funded advocacy initiatives supported structured planning and direct engagement with decision-makers. These efforts strengthened accountability practices, increased recognition of community demands, and fostered incremental improvements in services and protections, reinforcing community ownership and safer advocacy
